Theme

Latin word

cēterī

cēterī, cēterae, cētera

adjective, mostly plural, declension

everyone else, the rest, the others; the others, all the rest

In this lexicon

  • else

    also used · classical

  • the others

    the recommended word · classical · Plin. Ep. 9.33.4: audentior cēterīs; Sen. Ep. 15.10: quid tibi cum cēterīs?

Examples

  • hōc certāmine puer quīdam audentior cēterīs in ulteriōra tendēbat

    in this contest one boy, bolder than the others, kept swimming further outPlin. Ep. 9.33.4

    In the entry for the others

  • quid tibi cum cēterīs? tē ipse antecessistī

    what are the others to you? you have outrun yourselfSen. Ep. 15.10

    In the entry for the others

  • nec sibi sōlī, sed conjugī, līberīs cēterīsque, quōs cārōs habeat tuērīque dēbeat

    not for himself alone, but for his wife, his children and the others whom he holds dear and ought to protectCic. Off. 1.12

    In the entry for the others

  • sacrum Sōlī id animal et ōre ac distīnctū pinnārum ā cēterīs avibus dīversum

    the bird is sacred to the Sun, and differs from all the others in its beak and the markings of its feathersTac. Ann. 6.28

    In the entry for the others
